Dumping filters aim at eliminating the downward pressure of clearance
prices on the index.\

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Introduction {#Dumpingfilter-Introduction}

Dumping filters aim at eliminating the downward pressure of clearance
prices on the index. This is an issue especially when the index
calculation is conducted at the variety level such as, GTIN or any other
unique product identifier. In this case, new products will affect the
results of the majority of the relevant index formulas only poorly or
even not at all in the period of appearance. However, especially in the
case of relaunches, these products should have an immediate impact on
the index, which then in theory should balance out the downward pressure
of clearance prices. A dumping filter can therefore be of help in cases
where products leaving the market and products entering the market
cannot be linked appropriately.

It has to be remarked that the efficiency of the dumping filter depends
on the typical pricing strategy of the products for which the index is
calculated. For example, a dumping filter will not prevent a downward
bias of those products for which usually a price skimming strategy is
applied (e.g. clothing or electronic devices which are often introduced
at high initial prices and then dropped over time). For this situation,
it is absolutely essential to build homogeneous products groups first
(and not calculate on the GTIN level) (see section [Identifying unique
products](identifying-unique-products.qmd)) in order to
capture the price increasing effect of product relaunches and the
entrance of new products in general.

In general though, applying a dumping filter before the index
compilation can be helpful even when items have been grouped together in
a first step.

# Dumping filter for scanner data {#Dumpingfilter-Dumpingfilterforscannerdata}

Dumping filters are designed to detect and delete clearance sales which
are characterised by both a sharp decrease in prices and sales
quantities compared to the previous period. Scanner data provide the
information required to apply the dumping filter. Similar to the outlier
filter, a dumping filter should be set with caution. It has to be noted
that if both an outlier filter and a dumping filter are used, the
threshold value for the tolerated price decrease should be higher for
the outlier filter than for the dumping filter. Otherwise, the dumping
filter has no impact at all.

The section on [current
practice](current-practice-of-data-filtering.qmd) has some
examples of values which countries have chosen for the dumping filter.
Products identified by the dumping filter in a month should also be
excluded in the following months if price and quantity remain similar.

There is ongoing research into whether some indices suffer more from
downward pressure from clearance prices than others (see section
[Methods for when expenditure data are
available](methods-for-when-expenditure-data-are-available.qmd)).
Several analyses have revealed that especially the GEKS index reacts
sensitive to product sell-offs (e.g. Chessa et al. (2017), and van Loon
and Roels (2018)). However, while van Loon and Roels (2018) found only
short-term deviations and similar long-term price trends, Chessa et al.
(2017) found a longer lasting bias. This divergence in findings can
possibly be explained by the fact that van Loon and Roels (2018)
analysed the effect of clearance prices on multilateral methods without
chaining (full window) whereas Chessa et al. (2017) applied the fixed
base monthly expanding method to calculate the index series. Overall,
the current evidence indicates that the impact of dumping filtering has
stronger impacts on the GEKS index than on other multilateral indices
such as Geary-Khamis (GK) or Weighted Time Product Dummy (WTPD).

# Dumping filter for web scraped data {#Dumpingfilter-Dumpingfilterforwebscrapeddata}

In contrast to scanner data, web scraped data do not contain information
on the quantities sold for an observed price. Some research has been
conducted in the recent years how clearance prices can be also detected
when using web scraped data. In general, when [proxy weights are
determined for web scraped
data](https://unstats.un.org/wiki/display/GWGSD/Deriving+proxy+weights+for+web+scraped+data),
a dumping filter for scanner data can be applied to web scraped data in
a similar way. In the case of web scraped data, the proxy weights could
replace the quantities in order to determine together with the price
whether a product has reached the sell-off phase.
